answers-lazy.comment: PINNED 2026-08-28. Twenty of two thousand rows, abandoned, fifty times over. The inference pin is ZERO and that zero is the case: bridge.pl's metta_node_guarded/2 reports what a job spent as that job's LAST event, reached only once the command has no more answers, so an abandoned job contributes nothing. A lazy path that began draining would report query-rows' 282622 and fail this row by four orders of magnitude, and the workload's own crossing bound fails first at 1600. Instructions carry the SIZE, since a counter fixed at zero cannot say whether twenty rows cost twenty rows' work or two thousand; most of what they price is the teardown, because leaving the loop early closes the cursor and destroys the engine behind it. Fifty abandonments rather than one because a two millisecond window spread 0.2763 percent across nine samples against a one percent band. The three flags already there make a run reproducible against ITSELF; this makes it reproducible against a CHANGED PROGRAM. `--predictable-gc-schedule` is deterministic given the same allocation sequence and the startup heap is part of that sequence, so growing any module the benchmark loads shifted where a collection landed inside the window. Measured rather than argued, by a probe that cannot possibly do work: four kilobytes of INERT COMMENTS added to src/theory.ts moved host-op from 900018262 to 933434511, a 3.7 percent phantom regression from text nothing executes, and the same probe against the settled heap moves the whole suite at most 0.18 percent (atom-intern), with host-op at 0.016 percent. The rows that went UP now carry the collections their own allocation causes instead of inheriting an accidental share of the startup heap's, which is why answers-lazy and query-rows rose while host-op and atom-intern fell. counter_policy: stats().inferences minimum of three and fixed two-point growth slopes decide; wall time advises
counter_policy_note: Inferences decide wherever the engine does the work and are identical run to run; retired instructions decide where the work is on the TypeScript side of the wire, where the engine counter cannot move; three cases straddle the boundary and pin both. Wall clock decides NOTHING here and is recorded for advice only: every number in this file was taken on a box under loadavg 9 with another gate running, where the inference rows were byte identical across nine samples and wall clock was not.
instruction_policy: perf instructions:u minimum of three, one percent noise allowance unless a row declares its own beside the measurement that justified it
repin_note: 2026-08-30 late re-pin (petta matcher adoption): the match door dropped its entry scan, C classifier and per-candidate acyclic_term for upstream's one answer-template test, and let/unify bind raw; every seat's match-path rows moved with those shared constants, min-of-3.
v8_flag_note: Every instructions row is measured under the v8_flags in the stamp. A Node process is not deterministic enough to gate on retired instructions without them: bare, one engine workload spread 29.48 percent over four rounds, --liftoff-only alone took it to 2.55 percent and named the mechanism as TurboFan tiering swipl-wasm up on background threads inside the window, and the full set reaches 0.027 percent. These rows therefore measure Liftoff-compiled WebAssembly and single-threaded V8 rather than the tier a long-lived process settles into, which is the right trade for a gate that reads the change [measured 2026-08-28].
